1	# sh-tea
2	
3	A transparent pipeline stage logger for stdin→stdout Unix filters. It's a
4	`tee` pun: `tea` sits in front of tools like `grep`, `sed`, `awk`, and `sort`,
5	and — when activated — quietly copies each stage's stdin to a temp file and
6	logs it, without touching the tool's actual stdout. Your pipeline runs
7	exactly as before; you just get a paper trail of what each stage saw.
8	
9	```
10	cmd | grep --tea error | sort | uniq -c | tail -20
11	```
12	
13	`grep` still does exactly what `grep` does. Somewhere under `/tmp` there is
14	now a copy of what `grep` had for stdin, and `./logs.csv` has a row pointing
15	at it.
16	
17	## Why
18	
19	Debugging a long pipeline usually means re-running it with `tee` spliced in
20	at every stage you're suspicious of, or adding `set -x` and hoping. `tea`
21	flips that: the wrapper is always there, so instead of re-running anything
22	you just look at what already got captured. It's aimed squarely at agentic
23	coding sessions (Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot CLI, etc.) chaining `nix eval`
24	/ `nix build` output through `grep -C 10 | sort | uniq | tail -100` — `tea`
25	auto-activates there so the intermediate stream is on disk by the time
26	something looks wrong, with zero change to the command that was run.
27	
28	## Naming: sh-tea vs tea
29	
30	This repo and its Nix flake package attribute are `sh-tea`. The installed
31	CLI, every environment variable, and the config directory are all just
32	`tea` — that's the tool's actual day-to-day identity, kept short because
33	you'll be typing `--tea` and reading `TEA_*` constantly. `sh-tea` also ships
34	on `PATH` as a plain alias: same binary, same flags, same config, just a
35	second name for anyone who typed the full project name out of habit. Not an
36	inconsistency — see `man tea`'s NOTES section.
37	
38	## Install / build
39	
40	Everything is built through the flake — there's no supported `cargo build`
41	path for the real package (it needs `TEA_DEFAULT_CONFIG` / `TEA_TOOLS_JSON`
42	wired up by Nix at wrap-build time):
43	
44	```
45	nix build .#sh-tea
46	```
47	
48	The result is a `symlinkJoin` of the `tea` CLI, the `sh-tea` alias, the man
49	page, shell completions, and one thin wrapper binary per wrapped tool (see
50	`tools.nix` for the full list — `grep`, `sed`, `awk`, `sort`, `head`, `tail`,
51	`cut`, `tr`, `wc`, `uniq`, `join`, `column`, ... 30-ish filters total).
52	`meta.mainProgram = "tea"`.
53	
54	As a flake input in another flake:
55	
56	```nix
57	inputs.sh-tea.url = "github:mikenrafter/sh-tea";
58	# ...
59	environment.systemPackages = [ sh-tea.packages.${system}.sh-tea ];
60	```
61	
62	Note the package is `lib.hiPrio`'d — its wrapper binaries are meant to win
63	over the real `coreutils`/`gnugrep`/etc. on `PATH`.
64	
65	## Using it
66	
67	Every wrapped tool takes three extra flags that `tea` consumes before
68	handing the rest straight to the real binary:
69	
70	| flag | effect |
71	|---|---|
72	| `--tea` | force logging on for this invocation |
73	| `--no-tea` / `--coffee` | force logging off for this invocation |
74	| (nothing) | fall back to config / auto-detect |
75	
76	```bash
77	# Force it on in a script
78	some-cmd | grep --tea pattern
79	
80	# Force it off in an interactive terminal that would otherwise auto-activate
81	some-cmd | grep --coffee pattern | head --coffee
82	
83	# Clean stdout for jq — status blurbs are already on stderr, --coffee is belt-and-braces
84	nix eval --json .#foo | jq .
85	
86	# CLAUDE.md-style build filter: tea captures the raw pre-filter stream
87	nix build .#nixosConfigurations.void.config.system.build.toplevel --no-link \
88	  2>&1 | grep error -C 10 | sort | uniq | tail -100
89	tea last     # path of the newest capture
90	tea show     # dump it
91	```
92	
93	When a wrapper activates it prints exactly one line to stderr (never
94	stdout), e.g.:
95	
96	```
97	[tea] --id 60 /tmp/tmp.XXXXXX.tea | tail -150
98	```
99	
100	Set `TEA_QUIET=1` to suppress that. `tee` and `cat` are deliberately **not**
101	wrapped — they're identity/fan-out and don't mutate the stream, so there's
102	nothing interesting to capture that isn't already visible.
103	
104	### CLI
105	
106	```
107	tea last            # print path of the most recent logfile
108	tea list            # dump ./logs.csv
109	tea show [id]       # print a logfile's contents (default: most recent)
110	tea config          # ensure ~/.config/tea/config.toml exists, print its path
111	tea which TOOL      # debug: would activation fire for TOOL right now, and why
112	                    # (at the shell prompt interactive=false is normal; pipe in:
113	                    #  (same evaluate_activation() gate as tea-wrap; use --piped
114	                    #  or echo x | tea which TOOL for pipeline preview)
115	```
116	
117	### When does it actually activate?
118	
119	Precedence, highest first (see `src/lib.rs::evaluate_activation`):
120	
121	1. `--coffee` / `--no-tea` — force off (wins over everything)
122	2. `--tea` — force on (wins over all env vars and auto-detect gates)
123	3. `TEA_OFF=1` — env force off
124	4. `TEA_FORCE=1` — env force on
125	5. config / auto-detect (only on **user pipeline stages** — see below):
126	   - agentic session (detected via env vars like `CURSOR_AGENT`, `CLAUDECODE`,
127	     `COPILOT_CLI`, `AEGIS`, `HERMES_AGENT`, or a parent process name match)
128	     → activates
129	   - interactive pipeline stage (stderr is a TTY, stdin is a pipe, and the stage
130	     is a user pipeline — under `TERM_PROGRAM` that requires `TEA_USER_PIPE=1`
131	     from the fish hook; when the parent is interactive fish (no `-c`), likewise.
132	     Otherwise parent-shell heuristics apply, with POSIX
133	     `sh`/`dash` and deep nesting (`SHLVL` ≥ 5 under `TERM_PROGRAM`) excluded)
134	     → activates when `default-interactive = true` in config (the default)
135	   - otherwise → no-op, zero extra stderr, real binary runs untouched
136	
137	`tea which TOOL` calls the **same** `evaluate_activation()` gate as `tea-wrap`.
138	`would_activate` and `outcome` come directly from that decision; the other
139	lines are the runtime signals collected during that single evaluation (not
140	recomputed separately).
141	
142	At the shell prompt, `stdin_tty=true` so `interactive_session=false` — that is
143	expected. To preview a pipeline stage, pass `--piped`, or run
144	`echo x | tea which TOOL` so stdin matches what the wrapped tool would see.
145	
146	Fish users: the sh-tea package installs a hook at
147	`share/fish/vendor_conf.d/tea-user-pipe.fish` that sets `TEA_USER_PIPE=1`
148	around interactive commands whose command line contains `|` (so plain `echo hi`
149	does not mark Warp's internal filters). Pipeline stages are then recognized even
150	when parent heuristics would miss them. Bash users can add an equivalent
151	DEBUG-trap snippet — see `hooks/tea-user-pipe.bash`.
152	
153	`--tea` / `--coffee` only work on the **tea-wrapped** binaries from this
154	package (they must be ahead of the real `grep`, `sed`, etc. on `PATH`). The
155	wrapper strips the flag before execing the real tool; passing `--tea` to an
156	unwrapped system binary will fail.
157	
158	Fish ships a built-in `grep` **function** (with `--color=auto`) that shadows
159	PATH wrappers — only `grep` among sh-tea's tools; nothing else overlaps.
160	The package installs `share/fish/vendor_functions.d/grep.fish`, which
161	autoloads before embedded `grep.fish` and delegates via `command grep` so
162	the tea wrapper on PATH is used. Until that loads, use `command grep`.
163	
164	Tab completion is a separate fish issue: helpers like `__fish_complete_pids`
165	(run when completing `kill`, etc.) pipe to `tail -n +2` and otherwise look
166	like user pipeline stages. Tea ignores fish-parented stages unless
167	`TEA_USER_PIPE=1` from the preexec hook — the same marker real typed pipes use.
168	
169	Background systemd units (`INVOCATION_ID` set and stderr not a TTY)
170	suppress activation. User-session processes (shells, terminals) inherit
171	`INVOCATION_ID` from `user@.service` but keep stderr on a TTY, so they
172	are not suppressed. `TEA_INTERACTIVE=1` bypasses suppression.
173	
174	### Config
175	
176	`~/.config/tea/config.toml` (or `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/tea/config.toml`),
177	auto-created on first use with a `[tools.<name>]` section per wrapped tool.
178	Defaults, from the `[defaults]` block:
179	
180	```toml
181	default-interactive = true   # activate in interactive terminals without --tea
182	manual-only = false          # if true, ONLY --tea/TEA_FORCE activates
183	update-gitignore = true      # append logs.csv to .gitignore in a git work tree
184	max-log-records = 20         # rows kept in ./logs.csv; oldest + their .tea files pruned
185	quiet = false                # suppress the stderr blurb
186	only-in-git-repos = false    # restrict activation by git context
187	only-outside-git-repos = false
188	```
189	
190	Any key can be overridden per tool under `[tools.grep]`, `[tools.sort]`, etc.
191	
192	### Files & environment
193	
194	- `$TMPDIR/tmp.XXXXXX.tea` (usually `/tmp`) — one capture per activated
195	  stage, created with `mktemp --suffix .tea`. Ephemeral by design.
196	- `./logs.csv` — index of the last N stages (`id, timestamp, cwd, tool,
197	  command, highlighted, logfile, bytes, exit_code`). The `highlighted`
198	  column marks the active stage with `⟦...⟧` inside a best-effort
199	  reconstruction of its pipeline siblings.
200	- `TEA_OFF`, `TEA_FORCE` — env-level force off/on (CLI flags still win).
201	- `TEA_QUIET` — suppress the stderr blurb.
202	- `TEA_AGENT`, `TEA_INTERACTIVE` — force agentic/interactive detection.
203	- `TEA_USER_PIPE` — set by the fish hook (or manually) to mark user pipeline
204	  stages for auto-activation; does not bypass `--coffee` / `--no-tea`.
205	- `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` — config root (default `~/.config`).
206	
207	## Testing
208	
209	There's no `cargo test` — behavior is verified end to end against the real
210	Nix-built package:
211	
212	```
213	tests/functional.sh
214	```
215	
216	It builds `.#sh-tea` itself (or set `TEA_PKG=/nix/store/...` to point at an
217	already-built one) and drives it as a black box: activation precedence,
218	stdout passthrough, `logs.csv` indexing, `tea last|list|show|config`, the
219	announce format, and that `sh-tea` really is a working alias for `tea`. See
220	`tests/README.md` for the full contract summary.
221	
222	## Dev shell
223	
224	```
225	nix develop
226	```
227	
228	gives you `cargo`, `rustc`, `gcc`, and `rust-analyzer` for hacking on
229	`src/`. The actual package is still only ever built via `nix build .#sh-tea`
230	— the devshell is for editing/compiling, not for producing the shipped
231	binary.
232	
233	## Docs
234	
235	- `man tea` (also aliased as `man sh-tea`) — the authoritative reference for
236	  flags, activation order, config keys, files, and examples.
237	- `tools.nix` — canonical list of wrapped tools and why a few common ones
238	  (`tee`, `cat`, pagers, `split`/`csplit`, checksum tools, `dd`/`yes`/`seq`)
239	  are deliberately excluded.
240	
241	`tea` is intentionally weaker than a hypothetical `tapper(1)`: tapper would
242	be foresight, where you hand it the whole pipeline string up front. `tea` is
243	hindsight bolted onto habits you already have — no new command to learn,
244	and pipelines your agent already writes (`grep | sort | tail`) keep working
245	unmodified.
246

| `--no-tea` / `--coffee` | force logging off for this invocation |
| (nothing) | fall back to config / auto-detect |

```bash
# Force it on in a script
some-cmd | grep --tea pattern

# Force it off in an interactive terminal that would otherwise auto-activate
some-cmd | grep --coffee pattern | head --coffee

# Clean stdout for jq — status blurbs are already on stderr, --coffee is belt-and-braces
nix eval --json .#foo | jq .

# CLAUDE.md-style build filter: tea captures the raw pre-filter stream
nix build .#nixosConfigurations.void.config.system.build.toplevel --no-link \
  2>&1 | grep error -C 10 | sort | uniq | tail -100
tea last     # path of the newest capture
tea show     # dump it
```

When a wrapper activates it prints exactly one line to stderr (never
stdout), e.g.:

```
[tea] --id 60 /tmp/tmp.XXXXXX.tea | tail -150
```

Set `TEA_QUIET=1` to suppress that. `tee` and `cat` are deliberately **not**
wrapped — they're identity/fan-out and don't mutate the stream, so there's
nothing interesting to capture that isn't already visible.

### CLI

```
tea last            # print path of the most recent logfile
tea list            # dump ./logs.csv
tea show [id]       # print a logfile's contents (default: most recent)
tea config          # ensure ~/.config/tea/config.toml exists, print its path
tea which TOOL      # debug: would activation fire for TOOL right now, and why
                    # (at the shell prompt interactive=false is normal; pipe in:
                    #  (same evaluate_activation() gate as tea-wrap; use --piped
                    #  or echo x | tea which TOOL for pipeline preview)
```

### When does it actually activate?

Precedence, highest first (see `src/lib.rs::evaluate_activation`):

1. `--coffee` / `--no-tea` — force off (wins over everything)
2. `--tea` — force on (wins over all env vars and auto-detect gates)
3. `TEA_OFF=1` — env force off
4. `TEA_FORCE=1` — env force on
5. config / auto-detect (only on **user pipeline stages** — see below):
   - agentic session (detected via env vars like `CURSOR_AGENT`, `CLAUDECODE`,
     `COPILOT_CLI`, `AEGIS`, `HERMES_AGENT`, or a parent process name match)
     → activates
   - interactive pipeline stage (stderr is a TTY, stdin is a pipe, and the stage
     is a user pipeline — under `TERM_PROGRAM` that requires `TEA_USER_PIPE=1`
     from the fish hook; when the parent is interactive fish (no `-c`), likewise.
     Otherwise parent-shell heuristics apply, with POSIX
     `sh`/`dash` and deep nesting (`SHLVL` ≥ 5 under `TERM_PROGRAM`) excluded)
     → activates when `default-interactive = true` in config (the default)
   - otherwise → no-op, zero extra stderr, real binary runs untouched

`tea which TOOL` calls the **same** `evaluate_activation()` gate as `tea-wrap`.
`would_activate` and `outcome` come directly from that decision; the other
lines are the runtime signals collected during that single evaluation (not
recomputed separately).

At the shell prompt, `stdin_tty=true` so `interactive_session=false` — that is
expected. To preview a pipeline stage, pass `--piped`, or run
`echo x | tea which TOOL` so stdin matches what the wrapped tool would see.

Fish users: the sh-tea package installs a hook at
`share/fish/vendor_conf.d/tea-user-pipe.fish` that sets `TEA_USER_PIPE=1`
around interactive commands whose command line contains `|` (so plain `echo hi`
does not mark Warp's internal filters). Pipeline stages are then recognized even
when parent heuristics would miss them. Bash users can add an equivalent
DEBUG-trap snippet — see `hooks/tea-user-pipe.bash`.

`--tea` / `--coffee` only work on the **tea-wrapped** binaries from this
package (they must be ahead of the real `grep`, `sed`, etc. on `PATH`). The
wrapper strips the flag before execing the real tool; passing `--tea` to an
unwrapped system binary will fail.

Fish ships a built-in `grep` **function** (with `--color=auto`) that shadows
PATH wrappers — only `grep` among sh-tea's tools; nothing else overlaps.
The package installs `share/fish/vendor_functions.d/grep.fish`, which
autoloads before embedded `grep.fish` and delegates via `command grep` so
the tea wrapper on PATH is used. Until that loads, use `command grep`.

Tab completion is a separate fish issue: helpers like `__fish_complete_pids`
(run when completing `kill`, etc.) pipe to `tail -n +2` and otherwise look
like user pipeline stages. Tea ignores fish-parented stages unless
`TEA_USER_PIPE=1` from the preexec hook — the same marker real typed pipes use.

Background systemd units (`INVOCATION_ID` set and stderr not a TTY)
suppress activation. User-session processes (shells, terminals) inherit
`INVOCATION_ID` from `user@.service` but keep stderr on a TTY, so they
are not suppressed. `TEA_INTERACTIVE=1` bypasses suppression.

### Config

`~/.config/tea/config.toml` (or `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/tea/config.toml`),
auto-created on first use with a `[tools.<name>]` section per wrapped tool.
Defaults, from the `[defaults]` block:

```toml
default-interactive = true   # activate in interactive terminals without --tea
manual-only = false          # if true, ONLY --tea/TEA_FORCE activates
update-gitignore = true      # append logs.csv to .gitignore in a git work tree
max-log-records = 20         # rows kept in ./logs.csv; oldest + their .tea files pruned
quiet = false                # suppress the stderr blurb
only-in-git-repos = false    # restrict activation by git context
only-outside-git-repos = false
```

Any key can be overridden per tool under `[tools.grep]`, `[tools.sort]`, etc.

### Files & environment

- `$TMPDIR/tmp.XXXXXX.tea` (usually `/tmp`) — one capture per activated
  stage, created with `mktemp --suffix .tea`. Ephemeral by design.
- `./logs.csv` — index of the last N stages (`id, timestamp, cwd, tool,
  command, highlighted, logfile, bytes, exit_code`). The `highlighted`
  column marks the active stage with `⟦...⟧` inside a best-effort
  reconstruction of its pipeline siblings.
- `TEA_OFF`, `TEA_FORCE` — env-level force off/on (CLI flags still win).
- `TEA_QUIET` — suppress the stderr blurb.
- `TEA_AGENT`, `TEA_INTERACTIVE` — force agentic/interactive detection.
- `TEA_USER_PIPE` — set by the fish hook (or manually) to mark user pipeline
  stages for auto-activation; does not bypass `--coffee` / `--no-tea`.
- `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` — config root (default `~/.config`).

## Testing

There's no `cargo test` — behavior is verified end to end against the real
Nix-built package:

```
tests/functional.sh
```

It builds `.#sh-tea` itself (or set `TEA_PKG=/nix/store/...` to point at an
already-built one) and drives it as a black box: activation precedence,
stdout passthrough, `logs.csv` indexing, `tea last|list|show|config`, the
announce format, and that `sh-tea` really is a working alias for `tea`. See
`tests/README.md` for the full contract summary.

## Dev shell

```
nix develop
```

gives you `cargo`, `rustc`, `gcc`, and `rust-analyzer` for hacking on
`src/`. The actual package is still only ever built via `nix build .#sh-tea`
— the devshell is for editing/compiling, not for producing the shipped
binary.

## Docs

- `man tea` (also aliased as `man sh-tea`) — the authoritative reference for
  flags, activation order, config keys, files, and examples.
- `tools.nix` — canonical list of wrapped tools and why a few common ones
  (`tee`, `cat`, pagers, `split`/`csplit`, checksum tools, `dd`/`yes`/`seq`)
  are deliberately excluded.

`tea` is intentionally weaker than a hypothetical `tapper(1)`: tapper would
be foresight, where you hand it the whole pipeline string up front. `tea` is
hindsight bolted onto habits you already have — no new command to learn,
and pipelines your agent already writes (`grep | sort | tail`) keep working
unmodified.

content.text:
Short answer: **no**, not in the general case, and not without new instrumentation.

`tea-wrap` runs *as* the `grep` process (it execs and spawns the real `grep` as its own child). It only has:
1. **Its own timing** — trivial to measure (wrap `Instant::now()` around spawn/wait in `tea_wrap.rs`).
2. **A momentary `/proc` snapshot of pipeline siblings** — `discover_pipeline_siblings()` (`src/lib.rs:949`) already walks `/proc` for processes sharing its process group, for the highlight display. But that only tells you who's *currently alive* at the instant it's called, not how long a sibling ran in total.

`echo hi` is the real blocker: it's not a child of `grep`/`tea-wrap` — it's a sibling spawned by the same shell, so only the shell can `wait4()` it and get real elapsed time. And for a fast producer like `echo`, it typically finishes and exits **before `grep` even starts reading**, since a small pipe write doesn't block. By the time `tea-wrap` looks at `/proc`, `echo`'s PID may already be gone — there's no historical duration to read, only a live snapshot if you happen to poll while it's still running.

So "min time the upstream stage was running" would require either continuous polling of `/proc/<pid>/stat` for every sibling for as long as they exist (racy, adds latency, easy to miss the exit) or a shared timestamp mechanism where every wrapped tool records its own start/end somewhere the next stage can read — which is a real design addition, not a config knob.

What's actually easy and probably gets you most of what you want: gate on **the wrapped tool's own runtime** (e.g. don't log/announce if `grep` itself finished in under N ms) — cheap, no cross-process guessing. Want me to scope it that way instead, or do you specifically need upstream-producer timing (which would need the start/end-timestamp file approach)?

content.text: Let's say I ran `nixos-rebuild switch | grep error`... Wouldn't the grep pipe last a long time? Wouldn't it see a lengthy and time-consuming stdout stream?

You're right — that's the case where it actually works well, and it corrects the framing from before.

The key detail: `tea-wrap`'s stdin-copy loop (`copy_stdin_to_proc_and_log` in `src/lib.rs:1329`) blocks on `read()` until it hits EOF, and EOF only arrives when `nixos-rebuild switch` closes its stdout (i.e., when it exits). So for a *streaming* producer, `tea-wrap`'s own wall-clock time — from spawn to `child.wait()` — is bounded below by roughly the producer's total runtime, since grep literally cannot finish until nixos-rebuild is done writing. No cross-process `/proc` introspection needed; it's just how long the wrapper itself is alive.

The `echo hi` case is the opposite extreme: the producer writes its whole output into the pipe buffer and exits near-instantly, so grep's own elapsed time is ~0ms too — same signal, correctly discriminating.

So a **min-duration** config gate is very feasible, but it has to work as a *post-hoc* filter, not a pre-activation one:

- Activation still decides *whether to tee at all* (unchanged, still pre-spawn).
- Add wall-clock timing around the spawn→wait span in `run_wrapped` (`src/bin/tea_wrap.rs:21`).
- After the child exits, if elapsed < configured `min-duration-ms`, skip `register_log`/`announce` (or write the row but discard the logfile) instead of always logging.

This can't be decided *before* running (you don't know duration until it's over), but since tea already always tees when activated, the only change is making the logging step conditional on measured duration. Want me to scope this into a concrete plan (config key, CLI surface, `tea which` reporting) or just implement it directly?

229	run_capture env -u TEA_OFF TEA_FORCE=1 TEA_QUIET=1 "$TEA_OUT/bin/head" -n 2 <"$WORKDIR/stdin.txt"
230	if [[ "$CAPTURED_RC" -eq 0 && "$CAPTURED_OUT" == "$EXPECTED_HEAD" && "$(count_logs)" -ge 1 ]]; then
231	  pass "TEA_FORCE=1 forces on"
232	else
233	  fail "TEA_FORCE=1 should log (rc=$CAPTURED_RC logs=$(count_logs))"
234	fi
235	
236	# TEA_OFF wins over TEA_FORCE
237	clear_logs
238	run_capture env -u TEA_OFF TEA_OFF=1 TEA_FORCE=1 TEA_QUIET=1 "$TEA_OUT/bin/head" -n 2 <"$WORKDIR/stdin.txt"
239	if [[ "$(count_logs)" -eq 0 && ! -f "$WORKDIR/logs.csv" ]]; then
240	  pass "TEA_OFF wins over TEA_FORCE"
241	else
242	  fail "TEA_OFF should beat TEA_FORCE (logs=$(count_logs))"
243	fi

245	# --tea wins over TEA_OFF
246	clear_logs
247	run_capture env -u TEA_OFF TEA_OFF=1 TEA_QUIET=1 "$TEA_OUT/bin/head" --tea -n 2 <"$WORKDIR/stdin.txt"
248	if [[ "$(count_logs)" -ge 1 ]]; then

252	fi

254	# --coffee wins over TEA_FORCE
255	clear_logs
256	run_capture env -u TEA_OFF TEA_FORCE=1 TEA_QUIET=1 "$TEA_OUT/bin/head" --coffee -n 2 <"$WORKDIR/stdin.txt"
257	if [[ "$(count_logs)" -eq 0 && ! -f "$WORKDIR/logs.csv" ]]; then

367	run_capture env -u TEA_OFF TEA_FORCE=1 "$TEA_OUT/bin/grep" --coffee '^alpha' <"$WORKDIR/grep-in.txt"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Functional contract suite for tea (transparent pipeline logger).
#
# Encodes behavioural contracts from man tea + original smoke validation.
# Build via nix (never cargo).
#
# Run (from repo root):
#   tests/functional.sh
#
# Optional: TEA_PKG=/nix/store/... tests/functional.sh
set -euo pipefail

NIX="${NIX:-nix}"
REPO="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"

# Harness tools must not go through tea wrappers (agent sessions auto-activate).
SYS_BIN="${TEA_TEST_SYS_BIN:-/run/current-system/sw/bin}"
GREP="${SYS_BIN}/grep"
MKTEMP="${SYS_BIN}/mktemp"
RM="${SYS_BIN}/rm"
WC="${SYS_BIN}/wc"
TR="${SYS_BIN}/tr"
CAT="${SYS_BIN}/cat"
HEAD="${SYS_BIN}/head"
TAIL="${SYS_BIN}/tail"
MKDIR="${SYS_BIN}/mkdir"
BASENAME="${SYS_BIN}/basename"

failures=0
pass() { printf 'PASS: %s\n' "$1"; }
fail() {
  printf 'FAIL: %s\n' "$1" >&2
  failures=$((failures + 1))
}

if ! command -v "$NIX" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "FAIL: '$NIX' not found on PATH (set NIX=... to override)" >&2
  exit 2
fi

resolve_tea_pkg() {
  if [[ -n "${TEA_PKG:-}" ]]; then
    printf '%s' "$TEA_PKG"
    return
  fi
  (cd "$REPO" && "$NIX" build --no-link --print-out-paths --no-write-lock-file '.#sh-tea')
}

# Absolute logfile paths recorded in ./logs.csv (skip header).
# logfile is third-from-last column (…,logfile,bytes,exit_code); test rows
# keep earlier fields comma-free so a simple split is enough.
list_log_paths() {
  if [[ ! -f "$WORKDIR/logs.csv" ]]; then
    return 0
  fi
  "$TAIL" -n +2 "$WORKDIR/logs.csv" | while IFS= read -r row; do
    [[ -z "$row" ]] && continue
    path="$(printf '%s' "$row" | awk -F',' '{print $(NF-2)}')"
    [[ -n "$path" ]] && printf '%s\n' "$path"
  done
}

count_logs() {
  list_log_paths | "$WC" -l | "$TR" -d ' '
}

# Capture stdout without bash stripping trailing newlines (cmdsubst pitfall).
# Sets CAPTURED_OUT, CAPTURED_ERR, CAPTURED_RC.
run_capture() {
  local out_tmp err_tmp
  out_tmp="$("$MKTEMP" "$WORKDIR/out.XXXXXX")"
  err_tmp="$("$MKTEMP" "$WORKDIR/err.XXXXXX")"
  set +e
  "$@" >"$out_tmp" 2>"$err_tmp"
  CAPTURED_RC=$?
  set -e
  CAPTURED_OUT="$("$CAT" "$out_tmp"; printf x)"
  CAPTURED_OUT="${CAPTURED_OUT%x}"
  CAPTURED_ERR="$("$CAT" "$err_tmp"; printf x)"
  CAPTURED_ERR="${CAPTURED_ERR%x}"
  "$RM" -f "$out_tmp" "$err_tmp"
}

clear_logs() {
  if [[ -f "$WORKDIR/logs.csv" ]]; then
    while IFS= read -r path; do
      [[ -n "$path" && -f "$path" ]] && "$RM" -f "$path"
    done < <(list_log_paths)
  fi
  "$RM" -rf "$WORKDIR/logfiles" "$WORKDIR/logs.csv"
}

isolate_env() {
  export HOME="$WORKDIR/home"
  export XDG_CONFIG_HOME="$WORKDIR/xdg"
  unset TEA_FORCE TEA_AGENT TEA_INTERACTIVE TEA_USER_PIPE || true
  for v in CURSOR_AGENT CURSOR_AGENT_ID CURSOR_INVOKED_AS CLAUDECODE CLAUDE_CODE \
    CLAUDE_AGENT COPILOT_CLI COPILOT_AGENT AEGIS AEGIS_QUEUE HERMES_AGENT \
    HERMES_PROFILE AGENT_TASK_ID OPENCODE_AGENT AGENT; do
    unset "$v" || true
  done
  # Prefer tea wrappers under test; harness uses SYS_BIN absolutes.
  export PATH="$TEA_OUT/bin:$SYS_BIN:/usr/bin:/bin"
  # Keep harness PATH lookups from auto-logging into WORKDIR.
  export TEA_OFF=1
  unset TEA_QUIET || true
}

echo "== build tea package =="
TEA_OUT="$(resolve_tea_pkg)"
if [[ -z "$TEA_OUT" || ! -d "$TEA_OUT/bin" ]]; then
  echo "FAIL: tea package missing bin/ (got: ${TEA_OUT:-empty})" >&2
  exit 2
fi
pass "tea package at $TEA_OUT"

for need in tea sh-tea head grep; do
  if [[ ! -e "$TEA_OUT/bin/$need" ]]; then
    echo "FAIL: missing $TEA_OUT/bin/$need" >&2
    exit 2
  fi
done

WORKDIR="$("$MKTEMP" -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/tea-functional.XXXXXX")"
cleanup() { clear_logs; "$RM" -rf "$WORKDIR"; }
trap cleanup EXIT

"$MKDIR" -p "$WORKDIR/home" "$WORKDIR/xdg"
cd "$WORKDIR"
isolate_env

INPUT=$'alpha\nbeta\ngamma\n'
EXPECTED_HEAD=$'alpha\nbeta\n'
# Pattern must not match every line (beta/gamma both contain the letter a).
EXPECTED_GREP=$'alpha\n'

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# A. Activation / passthrough
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
echo "== A. activation / passthrough =="

clear_logs
printf '%s' "$INPUT" >"$WORKDIR/stdin.txt"

# --tea forces logging even with stderr redirected (non-interactive).
run_capture env -u TEA_OFF TEA_QUIET=1 "$TEA_OUT/bin/head" --tea -n 2 <"$WORKDIR/stdin.txt"
if [[ "$CAPTURED_RC" -eq 0 ]]; then
  pass "--tea activates (exit 0) with stderr redirected"
else
  fail "--tea exit $CAPTURED_RC (stderr redirected)"
fi
if [[ "$CAPTURED_OUT" == "$EXPECTED_HEAD" ]]; then
  pass "--tea preserves filter stdout (head -n 2)"
else
  fail "--tea stdout: expected $(printf %q "$EXPECTED_HEAD"), got $(printf %q "$CAPTURED_OUT")"
fi
if [[ -f "$WORKDIR/logs.csv" && "$(count_logs)" -ge 1 && ! -d "$WORKDIR/logfiles" ]]; then
  pass "--tea created logs.csv + .tea capture (no logfiles/)"
else
  fail "--tea did not create expected index/capture (csv=$([ -f "$WORKDIR/logs.csv" ] && echo y || echo n) logs=$(count_logs) logfiles=$([ -d "$WORKDIR/logfiles" ] && echo y || echo n))"
fi

# Status blurbs on stderr only; TEA_QUIET suppresses.
clear_logs
run_capture env -u TEA_OFF "$TEA_OUT/bin/head" --tea -n 2 <"$WORKDIR/stdin.txt"
if [[ "$CAPTURED_OUT" == "$EXPECTED_HEAD" ]]; then
  pass "stdout clean without TEA_QUIET (blurb not on stdout)"
else
  fail "stdout polluted without TEA_QUIET: $(printf %q "$CAPTURED_OUT")"
fi
if [[ "$CAPTURED_ERR" == *'[tea]'* ]]; then
  pass "status blurb on stderr when not quiet"
else
  fail "expected [tea] blurb on stderr, got $(printf %q "$CAPTURED_ERR")"
fi
# Single-line form: [tea] --id N /path/tmp.XXXX.tea | COMMAND
if [[ "$CAPTURED_ERR" =~ \[tea\]\ --id\ [0-9]+\ .+\.tea\ \|\  ]]; then
  pass "blurb matches '[tea] --id N …\.tea | COMMAND'"
else
  fail "blurb shape unexpected: $(printf %q "$CAPTURED_ERR")"
fi

clear_logs
run_capture env -u TEA_OFF TEA_QUIET=1 "$TEA_OUT/bin/head" --tea -n 2 <"$WORKDIR/stdin.txt"
if [[ -z "$CAPTURED_ERR" || "$CAPTURED_ERR" != *'[tea]'* ]]; then
  pass "TEA_QUIET=1 suppresses stderr blurb"
else
  fail "TEA_QUIET=1 still printed blurb: $(printf %q "$CAPTURED_ERR")"
fi

# --coffee / --no-tea passthrough
clear_logs
# Seed one log so we can detect "no new logfile".
run_capture env -u TEA_OFF TEA_QUIET=1 "$TEA_OUT/bin/head" --tea -n 1 <"$WORKDIR/stdin.txt"
before="$(count_logs)"
printf 'noop\n' >"$WORKDIR/coffee-in.txt"
run_capture env -u TEA_OFF TEA_FORCE=1 "$TEA_OUT/bin/head" --coffee -n 1 <"$WORKDIR/coffee-in.txt"
after="$(count_logs)"
if [[ "$CAPTURED_RC" -eq 0 && "$CAPTURED_OUT" == $'noop\n' ]]; then
  pass "--coffee preserves stdout"
else
  fail "--coffee failed (rc=$CAPTURED_RC out=$(printf %q "$CAPTURED_OUT"))"
fi
if [[ "$after" -eq "$before" ]]; then
  pass "--coffee did not create a new logfile"
else
  fail "--coffee created logfile (before=$before after=$after)"
fi

before="$(count_logs)"
run_capture env -u TEA_OFF TEA_FORCE=1 "$TEA_OUT/bin/head" --no-tea -n 1 <"$WORKDIR/coffee-in.txt"
after="$(count_logs)"
if [[ "$CAPTURED_RC" -eq 0 && "$CAPTURED_OUT" == $'noop\n' && "$after" -eq "$before" ]]; then
  pass "--no-tea forces passthrough (no new logfile)"
else
  fail "--no-tea failed (rc=$CAPTURED_RC after=$after before=$before out=$(printf %q "$CAPTURED_OUT"))"
fi

# TEA_OFF / TEA_FORCE; flags win over env
clear_logs
run_capture env -u TEA_OFF TEA_OFF=1 TEA_QUIET=1 "$TEA_OUT/bin/head" -n 2 <"$WORKDIR/stdin.txt"
if [[ "$CAPTURED_OUT" == "$EXPECTED_HEAD" && "$(count_logs)" -eq 0 && ! -f "$WORKDIR/logs.csv" ]]; then
  pass "TEA_OFF=1 forces off (no logfile)"
else
  fail "TEA_OFF=1 should not log (logs=$(count_logs) csv=$([ -f "$WORKDIR/logs.csv" ] && echo y || echo n))"
fi

clear_logs

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# duration-watcher-pipe: proves the mechanism tea-wrap would rely on —
# a stage that blocks reading stdin until EOF has an elapsed wall-clock
# time bounded below by the upstream producer's runtime, because EOF only
# arrives when the producer closes its stdout (usually at exit).
#
# Usage: <producer> | duration-watcher-pipe.sh MIN_SECONDS
set -euo pipefail
min="${1:?usage: duration-watcher-pipe.sh MIN_SECONDS}"

start=$(date +%s.%N)
cat >/dev/null   # stand-in for copy_stdin_to_proc_and_log's read loop
end=$(date +%s.%N)
elapsed=$(awk -v a="$start" -v b="$end" 'BEGIN{printf "%.3f", b-a}')

if awk -v e="$elapsed" -v m="$min" 'BEGIN{exit !(e>=m)}'; then
  echo "PASS elapsed=${elapsed}s >= min=${min}s"
  exit 0
else
  echo "FAIL elapsed=${elapsed}s < min=${min}s"
  exit 1
fi

# AGENTS.md — phoe-nix agent orientation

This is a NixOS flake managing two hosts:
- **void** (x86_64-linux): primary workstation + orchestration host
- **nixed** (aarch64-linux, Asahi/M1): comms server + local inference node

## Key directories:
- `hosts/` — per-host NixOS configuration
- `modules/` — reusable NixOS modules
- `knowledge/` — agent memory, procedures, wisdom (not NixOS config)
- `home/` — Home Manager configuration

## Active branch: hermes-orchestration-stack

## Before making any NixOS change:
1. Check `knowledge/procedures/` for validated workflows
2. Make the change in the appropriate module or host file
3. Test with `nix flake check --no-build`
4. Commit the change
5. Rebuild with `sudo nixos-rebuild switch --flake .#void` (or `#nixed`)

## Module ownership:
- `modules/litellm.nix` — LiteLLM routing proxy (v0id.litellm)
- `modules/hermes.nix` — Hermes agent harness (v0id.hermes / services.hermes-agent)
- `modules/matrix.nix` — Matrix/Conduit on nixed (v0id.matrix)
- `modules/llama-server.nix` — llama.cpp inference on nixed (v0id.llamaServer)
- `modules/aegis/` — Aegis meta-harness TUI (v0id.aegis)
- `modules/agent-tools.nix` — llm-agents.nix overlay packages
- `modules/ollama.nix` — Ollama local inference on void
- `scout-modules/tea/` — tea transparent pipeline logger (scout module, packages.scout facet; wraps stdin→stdout filters)

## SOPS secrets:
- void: `/etc/secrets/void.yaml` (anthropic_api_key, openrouter_api_key, litellm_master_key)
- nixed: `/etc/secrets/nixed.yaml` (matrix_registration_secret, matrix_admin_password)
- Age key derived from SSH host key via sops-nix

## Hermes agents (soul files in knowledge/agents/):
- `lore` — top-level orchestrator; delegates to specialists
- `data` — systems operations, NixOS, monitoring, backups
- `scotty` — software development, builds, Nix packaging
- `dax` — research, analysis, world awareness, feeds
- `uhura` — communications, Matrix alerts, message routing
- `number-one` — daily operations, general assistance, first contact
- `majel` — content creation, writing, knowledge curation

## Aegis meta-harness:
- Config: `.aegis.yaml` at repo root
- Run from repo root: `aegis`
- Providers registered: `claude-code`, `claude-code-fast`, `copilot`
- Queues: `main` (claude-code, 1x), `fast` (haiku, 2x), `copilot-tasks` (1x)
- Group presets: `all-agents`, `ops`
- Schedules: `morning-briefing-data`, `morning-briefing-summary` (disabled by default)

## Agent skills (Niri GLSL / profiling)

Canonical skills live in `.agents/skills/` ([agentskills.io](https://agentskills.io) format). Symlinked for:

| Tool | Path |
|------|------|
| Cursor | `.cursor/skills/` |
| Claude Code | `.claude/skills/` |
| Copilot CLI | `.github/skills/` |
| OpenCode | `.opencode/skills/` |

| Skill | Use when |

| `igpu-glsl-trig` | `fast_sincos`, iGPU sin/cos cost |

- Commit `.env` files or raw API keys
- Use `nixos-rebuild` without committing first
- Run `rm -rf` on Nix store paths
